title: automate KMS/HSM TLS rotation for private-installer + helm/terraform updates (Vault + SealedSecrets integration)
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require automated lifecycle management for crypto material (TLS certs and KMS/HSM keys) to meet our SLAs and reduce manual ops for customers. This PR implements a cross-repo feature that automates TLS rotation and KMS/HSM key rolling in the private-installer flow and updates Helm charts and Terraform modules so customers can opt into Vault or SealedSecrets workflows.

What this changes: adds a new rotation controller and upgrade hooks to the private-installer; extends the Helm chart with rotationConfig and kmsProvider abstractions; Terraform modules gain new inputs for kms_provider (aws_kms|vault_hsm|cloud_hsm), sealed_secrets support, and extra bootstrap steps; docs and operator runbooks included. The implementation aims to be backward compatible by default (rotation disabled unless enabled in values / tf vars).

Key features: 1) Rotation controller: Kubernetes controller that watches Certificate resources and KMS key metadata to orchestrate safe rotations with staged rollouts and canary verification hooks. 2) HSM/KMS integration: support for AWS KMS, Vault (Transit + PKI), and Cloud HSM-backed keys with configurable key-versions and automated rewrap for sealed secrets and TLS private keys. 3) Secrets handling: optional SealedSecrets flow (sealed-secrets controller bootstrap + re-seal step) and Vault agent sidecar support for on-boot rehydration. 4) Helm chart changes: new values.hierarchy rotationConfig, kmsProvider settings, preUpgrade/postUpgrade hooks to run rotation health checks. 5) Terraform module updates: new resources and remote-exec scripts to bootstrap Vault policies, HSM key enrollment, and rotate schedules. 6) Upgrade/rollback tooling: idempotent pre-upgrade checks that ensure KV caches are drained, and a conservative rollback path to previous key-versions if verification fails.

Compatibility and safety: default is opt-in. For existing installations no changes occur unless the operator flips rotation.enabled=true and configures a kmsProvider. The controller uses a staged rollout (n pods at a time) and can run user-specified smoke tests between stages. All operations are logged and exposed via metrics for Redwood Console.

Testing & validation: unit tests for controller logic, e2e scenarios using kind + local HSM emulator and HashiCorp Vault dev server, Terraform plan validation and Helm linting. CI runs include integration against our private-installer acceptance harness.

Related: ENG-5421 designs the rotation controller; ENG-5980 tracked terraform contract changes for private deploys; SUP-2314 came from a customer incident where manual cert rotation caused downtime.

Notes: This PR touches installer UX and security-sensitive areas; reviewers should focus on controller replay-safety, RBAC scopes, and bootstrap docs.
